ABSTRACT

Prostate

cancer

(PCa)

is

the

second

most

lethal

cancer

among

men

in

Brazil,

and

is

potentially

curable

when

diagnosed

early.

The

resistance

of

the

male

public

to

adhering

to

preventive

practices

contributes

to

the

persistence

of

late

diagnoses

and

higher

mortality

rates,

even

though,

in

Brazil,

there

are

national

public

policies

aimed

at

prevention

and

free

treatment.

In

this

respect,

the

development

of

digital

systems

can

enable

the

active

search

for

men

susceptible

to

developing

prostate

cancer

and

their

connection

to

healthcare

services,

contributing

to

the

optimization

of

adherence

to

preventive

care.

With

the

aim

of

developing

a

prototype

graphical

interface

for

a

digital

platform

to

enable

the

management

of

prostate

cancer

preventive

care

in

Primary

Health

Care

(PHC),

a

methodological

study

was

carried

out

in

four

stages

–

(I)

Specification

of

requirements;

(II)

Structuring,

in

which

objectives

and

functionalities,

diagrams,

flowcharts

and

wireframes

were

defined;

(III)

Prototyping,

in

which

graphical

interfaces

were

created

and

interactions

between

them

were

developed;

and

(IV)

Evaluation,

in

which

the

prototype

was

evaluated

by

primary

health

care

professionals.

Twenty-four

functional

requirements

and

twelve

non-functional

requirements

were

listed,

in

addition

to

two

flowcharts,

thirteen

wireframes,

and

three

Use

Case

Diagrams,

which

represent

the

user's

interaction

with

the

system.

Furthermore,

the

medium-fidelity

prototype

entitled

SISNEO

offers

the

following

functionalities:

patient

registration,

application

of

the

International

Prostate

Symptom

Score,

appointment

scheduling,

patient

management,

control

of

exams

and

referrals,

and

generation

of

statistical

reports.

In

the

evaluation,

the

prototype

obtained

a

satisfactory

level

of

agreement

among

professionals,

indicating

that

it

could

be

implemented

in

primary

health

care,

as

well

as

assist

in

adherence

to

preventive

care

for

PCa.

The

prototype

developed

in

this

study

shows

potential

for

expanding

and

implementing

preventive

care,

with

an

emphasis

on

identifying

and

evaluating

individuals

susceptible

to

PCa,

and

can

also

contribute

to

managers'

decision-making

regarding

the

planning

of

actions

to

control

PCa

through

statistical

reports.

ABSTRACT

Prostate

cancer

(PCa)

is

the

second

most

lethal

cancer

among

men

in

Brazil,

and

is

potentially

curable

when

diagnosed

early.

The

resistance

of

the

male

public

to

adhering

to

preventive

practices

contributes

to

the

persistence

of

late

diagnoses

and

higher

mortality

rates,

even

though,

in

Brazil,

there

are

national

public

policies

aimed

at

prevention

and

free

treatment.

In

this

respect,

the

development

of

digital

systems

can

enable

the

active

search

for

men

susceptible

to

developing

prostate

cancer

and

their

connection

to

healthcare

services,

contributing

to

the

optimization

of

adherence

to

preventive

care.

With

the

aim

of

developing

a

prototype

graphical

interface

for

a

digital

platform

to

enable

the

management

of

prostate

cancer

preventive

care

in

Primary

Health

Care

(PHC),

a

methodological

study

was

carried

out

in

four

stages

–

(I)

Specification

of

requirements;

(II)

Structuring,

in

which

objectives

and

functionalities,

diagrams,

flowcharts

and

wireframes

were

defined;

(III)

Prototyping,

in

which

graphical

interfaces

were

created

and

interactions

between

them

were

developed;

and

(IV)

Evaluation,

in

which

the

prototype

was

evaluated

by

primary

health

care

professionals.

Twenty-four

functional

requirements

and

twelve

non-functional

requirements

were

listed,

in

addition

to

two

flowcharts,

thirteen

wireframes,

and

three

Use

Case

Diagrams,

which

represent

the

user's

interaction

with

the

system.

Furthermore,

the

medium-fidelity

prototype

entitled

SISNEO

offers

the

following

functionalities:

patient

registration,

application

of

the

International

Prostate

Symptom

Score,

appointment

scheduling,

patient

management,

control

of

exams

and

referrals,

and

generation

of

statistical

reports.

In

the

evaluation,

the

prototype

obtained

a

satisfactory

level

of

agreement

among

professionals,

indicating

that

it

could

be

implemented

in

primary

health

care,

as

well

as

assist

in

adherence

to

preventive

care

for

PCa.

The

prototype

developed

in

this

study

shows

potential

for

expanding

and

implementing

preventive

care,

with

an

emphasis

on

identifying

and

evaluating

individuals

susceptible

to

PCa,

and

can

also

contribute

to

managers'

decision-making

regarding

the

planning

of

actions

to

control

PCa

through

statistical

reports.
